title: Onramp Velocity Battlesheet — Seller Notes (Draft)
summary: Compact seller-facing deck and speaker notes aimed at accelerating pilot velocity for engineering-led trials. Focus: qualify fast, surface low-effort integration wins, set conservative SLOs, propose fallback policies, and close to a small reserved-capacity or proof-of-value by week 6.
target_audience: Sales engineers (SEs), account execs (AEs) with platform/infra buyers, early adopter product teams evaluating inference for production features.
objective: Enable a 20–30 minute pilot qualification call that results in: a defined success metric, a 6-week pilot plan, technical owner identified, and one committed integration checkpoint (demo or data stripe).
narrative_script: Open: 45s — Why speed matters: time-to-insight vs time-to-product. Say: 'We help teams go from concept to measurable inference in weeks, not months.'

Problem framing: 60s — Common early roadblocks (latency surprises, cost surprises, integration risk). Use quick anecdote: 'Shopify-like catalog search pilot: initial latency x3 — resolved by routing/quantization.'
Proposed path: 90s — Lightweight pilot path: sample dataset, 2 endpoints (low-latency + cost-optimized), 1 monitoring dashboard, fallback policy. Ask for commitment to a 6-week cadence.
Close: 30s — Clear next step asked for: intro to infra owner + a test data export or synthetic sample. 'If we get those, we can run a meaningful trial in 10 business days.'
slides_outline: 1 — Title + one-line hook: 'Pilot to production: measurable inference in 6 weeks'
2 — What we solve: three bullet problems (latency, cost unpredictability, integration friction)
3 — Quick wins map: integration touchpoints and expected lift (search relevance, summarization latency, embedding recall)
4 — Pilot mechanics: objectives, minimum inputs we need, roles, timeline (weeks 0–6)
5 — SLO & success metrics template: latency P95, cost per 1k queries, accuracy/regression threshold, user-impact KPI
6 — Fallback plan & risk controls: model variants, quantized fallbacks, regional routing, canary ramping
7 — Example ask script + data checklist for engineering owners
8 — Pricing preview & commit triggers: when to move to reserved capacity or private deployment
10 — Next steps & clear asks: roles, artifacts, meeting cadence
pilot-qualification-quick-questions: What is the user facing SLA for this feature today?
Estimate monthly QPS and expected peak patterns (burst vs steady)?
Is there PII in the payloads? (if yes -> private or dedicated + KMS conversation)
Who owns infra/networking for services that will call the API?
Can you provision a 1GB sample dataset or a synthetic equivalent?
technical-assumptions: We can stage a pilot on hosted Redwood API unless customer requires private/VPC (ask security early).
Typical pilot traffic profile: <200 QPS peak; for >200 QPS propose dedicated capacity sizing conversation.
Model variants will be used: latency-focused (lower max tokens, small model) and cost-focused (quantized variant) with automated routing.
We need a stable sample set to run baseline and regression checks (tokens, request size distribution).
success-metrics: Technical: P95 latency <= target (customer-defined), error rate <0.5% per endpoint
Economic: per-1k inference unit cost within agreed bound (±15%)
Product: measurable uplift in user metric (CTR, retention, time-saved) vs baseline
Operational: 2-week continuity with <1 incident requiring manual rollback
common-objections-and-responses: Objection: 'We can't share data.' — Response: Offer synthetic data + on-prem pilot option; propose encrypted test slice and NDA
Objection: 'We need predictable cost.' — Response: Start with a reserved micro-pool + Optimize recommendations; show cost simulation using their QPS profile
Objection: 'Latency is non-negotiable.' — Response: Propose a latency-first micro-route with smaller model and prefix caching; show historical P95 from similar pilots
Objection: 'Compliance/regulatory concerns.' — Response: Outline Private deployment option and audit log features; loop in security SME for specifics
fast-rollback-heuristics: If model error rate spikes >2% sustained for 5 minutes -> auto-fallback to canary model variant
If P95 latency degrades >2x baseline during business hours -> scale down batch size and route to latency variant
If cost per 1k tokens exceeds forecast by 30% in a rolling 24h window -> throttle non-critical routes and notify account team
next-steps: SE to run 20m technical qualifier using this sheet and capture answers in Pilot Intake form (link in artifacts)
Agree on pilot success metric and publish to shared tracking board by Friday
If private data is needed, start NDA + security intake within 48 hours
Schedule week-1 sandbox kickoff (engineering + product + SE) — target within 10 business days
references: Example case: anonymized retail search pilot (metrics slide deck id: RET-CASE-21)
notes-to-self: Keep anecdotes short. Prioritize two seller scripts: one for infra-first buyers and one for product-first buyers. Add small appendix later: sample curl command + minimal SDK snippet.
